# Rage of Morditas

by VisionGLLast Updated: October 1, 2026

### Advertisement

This website is supported by ads.

Rage of Morditas is a timed, multi-phase Random Encounter that starts when you find and interact with Blood Crystals in the Campaign or the Monolith of Fate. Completing these encounters opens a Rewards Panel where you can take or manipulate Rewards using the Bloodrage Charges you gain through participating in the mechanic. The Rage of Morditas mechanic has exclusive Item Subtypes and special Uniques called Variant Uniques. It's also how you challenge Morditas and eventually Pinnacle Morditas.

Rage of Morditas Mechanic Blood Crystal and Rewards Pannel

## What is Rage of Morditas?

Rage of Morditas
Rage of Morditas encounters begin appearing in the Campaign as early as Chapter 2, and you continue finding them all the way through the Monolith of Fate. Monolith of Fate Rage of Morditas encounters also feed into a progression system that eventually unlocks the boss fight against Morditas, and later on Pinnacle Morditas.

The Rage of Morditas encounter is marked by a Blood Crystal. When you enter an area with a Blood Crystal, a chat notification appears stating "Anger is building up in the air." The Blood Crystal is also marked on the minimap. The encounter only begins when you interact with the Blood Crystal. Activating the Blood Crystal summons a non-corporeal Shade of Morditas, and a countdown timer begins. This starts Phase One.

Blood Crystal Marking a Rage of Morditas Encounter

This is the basic Rage of Morditas Encounter Flow:

- Find and Activate a Blood Crystal.
- Kill enemies during the timed Phase One.
- Earn Bloodrage Charges and Bloodrage Buffs as you slay enemies.
- When the timer expires, Phase Two begins.
- Fight the revived enemies from Phase One to complete Phase Two.
- Interact with the Blood-Filled Crystal to spend Bloodrage Charges on Rewards or to perform Rituals.

## Interacting with the Rage of Morditas Mechanic

Rage of Morditas
The Rage of Morditas encounter takes place over two separate Phases. Phase One is a timed encounter where you traverse your current area and slay any enemies that you find. Phase Two begins when the countdown timer reaches zero. At the start of Phase Two, you are enclosed in an arena, and the Shade of Morditas revives every enemy slain during Phase One. As you slay enemies, you gain Bloodrage Buffs to help you and Bloodrage Charges, which you can use to purchase Rewards or perform Rituals when the Rage of Morditas encounter ends.

### Phase One

Phase One is the timed portion of the Rage of Morditas encounter, where you hunt enemies and build up Bloodrage Charges. In Campaign, the timer begins at 25 Seconds. Later, in the Monolith of Fate, the starting timer becomes 20 Seconds. This timer is extended as you slay enemies, with high-rarity enemies providing a larger extension to your remaining time.

Killing enemies in Phase One also counts toward Bloodrage Charge thresholds and produces Blood Souls for the nearby Shade of Morditas to collect. You can't interact with these Blood Souls directly. They are just a visual representation of you making progress in the encounter.

During Phase One, a trail of Blood Vapor points toward the nearest enemies. This helps you quickly locate your next targets to extend the encounter timer as you work toward raising your Bloodrage Charges. Once the timer runs out, Phase Two begins. You need to slay 200 enemies to max out your Bloodrage Charges, and reaching these 200 kills causes the timer to rapidly decrease to zero.

Blood Vapor Pointing to the Nearest Pack of Enemies

### Bloodrage Charges

You gain Bloodrage Charges at certain thresholds of Enemies slain during Phase One. They serve two functions. With each Bloodrage Charge you gain, you also gain a Bloodrage Buff. Finally, after completing Phase Two, each Bloodrage Charge also provides one Reward action.

Bloodrage Charge Thresholds:

- 1 Bloodrage Charge - 20 Kills
- 2 Bloodrage Charges - 50 Kills
- 3 Bloodrage Charges - 90 Kills
- 4 Bloodrage Charges - 140 Kills
- 5 Bloodrage Charges - 200 Kills

Your progress toward the next Bloodrage Charge is displayed on the encounter's Rage Bar. This Rage Bar has visual indicators for each threshold. You can receive up to five Bloodrage Charges. Going beyond 200 Kills does not provide additional Bloodrage Charges. Instead, the timer begins draining rapidly.

The Bloodrage Charges you gain during a Rage of Morditas encounter do not carry over to the next. You spend your Bloodrage Charges after Phase Two ends. You can spend your Bloodrage Charges to Claim a Reward, Perform a Frozen Ritual, or Perform a Bloody Ritual.

### Bloodrage Buffs

You gain Bloodrage Buffs with each Bloodrage Charge you acquire. There are 28 different types of Bloodrage Buffs. Each Bloodrage Charge threshold you reach randomly grants one Bloodrage Buff. Bloodrage Buffs are split into weighted Tiers that affect your likelihood of gaining certain ones. You cannot obtain the same Bloodrage Buff more than once during the same encounter.

Bloodrage Buffs last for the entire Rage of Morditas encounter. In addition to each Bloodrage Buff's special effect, each one also grants 5% Attack and Cast Speed and 3% Movement Speed. Some Bloodrage Buffs also have different eligibility requirements, such as requiring active Minions, or not having a source of Ward gained per Missing Health.

#### Bloodrage Buff List

##### Common

- Berserking Rage - You have Frenzy. 40% increased effect of Frenzy on you.

- Predator Rage - You have Haste. 40% increased effect of Haste on you.

- Eternal Rage - +50 Ward per second. 50% increased Mana Regeneration.

- Commanding Rage - (Requires Minions) Your Minions have Haste and Frenzy. 50% increased effect of Haste and Frenzy on your Minions.

- Explosive Rage - 50% increased Area of Effect for Area Skills

- Sanguine Rage - +200% Bleed chance and 100% increased Damage over Time.

- Feasting Rage - (Requires No Ward gain per missing Health) 10% of Damage Leeched as Health. 10% of Damage Leeched is also dealt to a nearby Enemy.

- Murderous Rage - Hits inflict Marked for Death

- Blighted Rage - (Requires Minions) When one of your Minions dies, they leave a Blood Rune on the ground that bursts after 1 second. Your Minions also have a 30% Chance on Kill to leave a Blood Rune on the ground under the Target.

- Freezing Rage - Every 2 seconds, you create a nova of Ice Projectiles that have a high Freeze Rate. 30% More Damage to Frozen Enemies.

- Boiling Rage - (Requires Minions) Your Minions have a Damaging Aura around them.

##### Less Common

- Incisive Rage - Critical Strikes have a 20% chance to be Deadly Strikes. +10% Critical Strike Chance.

- Empowered Rage - +10 to All Attributes

- Crescendoing Rage - Every third ability you cast deals 50% More Damage and has 100% increased Area of Effect.

- Bursting Rage - Enemies you kill explode in a Burst of Blood. This effect can chain.

- Icy Rage - Directly using an ability also fires a Bloodice Shard (up to 3 times per 2 seconds).

- Evasive Rage - When you use Evade, you scatter 5 Blood Runes underneath nearby Enemies that explode after 1 second.

- Revitalizing Rage - Enemies have a chance to drop a Blood Potion on death, or when hitting a Rare enemy or a Boss. Running over a Blood Potion consumes it as if it were a Potion, and increases your Movement Speed for 1 Second. Can only happen twice every 4 Seconds.

- Shattering Rage - (Requires Minions) If your Minions hit the same Target 5 times, it creates a Bloodice Explosion around the Target.

- Pack Rage - (Requires Minions) You and your Minions gain 2% increased Attack and Cast Speed for every other Ally within 12m, up to 40%.

##### Rare

- Frigid Rage - When you kill a Boss or Rare Enemy, Ice Ground forms under them, dealing damage over time. This effect also has a 10% chance to occur when hitting a Boss or Rare Enemy (up to 1 time every 10 seconds).

- Rippling Rage - Using a Traversal Skill creates 3 large Icy Shockwaves upon arrival.

- Fevered Rage - A Bloody Rage Aura around you dealing Damage over Time.

- Runic Rage - Every 6 Seconds while in Combat, a Rune is drawn on the ground that lasts 6 Seconds. Allies standing on the rune gain 20% increased Attack and Cast Speed, 20% More Damage, and their Skills cost 20% less Mana.

- Portentous Rage - After directly using a non-channeled, non-cooldown Ability, it is cast again after 1 Second. Can only happen once every Second.

- Coalescing Rage - Blood Orbs periodically appear around you and detonate when an Enemy touches them.

- Monstrous Rage - (Requires Minions) Every 3 seconds, one of your Minions is randomly buffed for 3 Seconds, granting them 25% More Damage and Haste. If they die, they explode in a large Burst.

- Reptilian Blood Rage - Loot Lizards have a chance to appear nearby.

### Phase Two: Gauntlet of Blood and Ice

Phase Two begins when the Phase One timer reaches zero. A short transition period occurs between Phases, where an arena forms around you. Enemies you killed during Phase One are revived and swarm you during Phase Two. Phase Two ends when you slay all revived enemies.

Completing Phase Two causes a Blood-Filled Crystal to appear. Interacting with the Blood-Filled Crystal opens the Reward Panel. You can cancel Phase Two by leaving the combat area for 4 Seconds.

Blood-Filled Crystal

## Rewards and Rituals

Rage of Morditas
Completing a Rage of Morditas encounter and interacting with the Blood-Filled Crystal opens the Rewards Panel and presents five Reward choices. You can take or manipulate these Rewards with Rituals by using your Bloodrage Charges. The Rage of Morditas mechanic is the only way to obtain items with Ice Forging Potential and Blood Forging Potential. Additionally, there are exclusive Item Subtypes and special Variant Uniques.

### Reward Panel

When you interact with the Blood-Filled Crystal, it presents 5 possible Rewards. In the beginning, four slots contain Equipment, and the final slot can contain Keys, Crafting Materials, Bags of Resources, and other rewards. Each Bloodrage Charge you gain during the Rage of Morditas encounter gives you one action you can perform within the Reward Panel. Claim the Reward, Perform a Frozen Ritual, or Perform a Bloody Ritual.

Selecting a Reward gives you the Reward and refreshes the Reward Panel, generating five new Rewards. Rituals reroll Rewards and affect their Quality, Quantity, or Item Types. Bloodrage Charges do not carry over between encounters. Your current Reward Panel does, however.

Rage of Morditas Rewards Panel

### Frozen Rituals

Frozen Rituals cost 1 Bloodrage Charge to perform. When you perform a Frozen Ritual, you sacrifice the Reward you have selected and remove it from the Reward Panel, along with the Reward Slot that contained it. In addition to this, all remaining Rewards in the Reward Panel are rerolled.

With the Frozen Ritual, all the newly rerolled Rewards are guaranteed to be the same Item Type as the sacrificed Reward. Equipment Rewards generated this way have a higher chance to generate with similar Affixes. Finally, Rare and Exalted Items generated through Frozen Rituals receive Ice Forging Potential in place of the usual Forging Potential.

#### Ice Forging Potential

Ice Forging Potential is a special type of Forging Potential that is associated with Frozen Rituals. It has a higher chance to be preserved when it would otherwise be consumed during Crafting. Frozen Rituals are the only way to obtain items with Ice Forging Potential.

Frozen Ritual

### Bloody Rituals

Bloody Ritual

You can spend 1 Bloodrage Charge to perform a Bloody Ritual. When you use a Bloody Ritual, you select one reward to sacrifice. When you sacrifice an item this way, the Reward and Reward Slot are removed from the Reward Panel, and all remaining Rewards are reolled.

The newly generated Rewards cannot be the same Item type as the sacrificed Reward. This exclusion remains active until a Reward is selected. Rare and Exalted Items generated through Bloody Rituals receive Blood Forging Potential.

#### Blood Forging Potential

Blood Forging Potential is a special type of Forging Potential associated with Bloody Rituals. It increases your Critical Success Chance when Crafting on the Item. This is the only way to obtain items with Blood Forging Potential.

## Rage of Morditas Exclusive Rewards

Rage of Morditas
There are 18 special Item Subtypes that you can only obtain through the Rage of Morditas mechanic. In addition to this, it's the only place to obtain the special Variant Uniques, Withstand the Elements and Unsated Rage, other than from fighting Morditas or Pinnacle Morditas.

### Variant Unique Items

The Rage of Morditas mechanic can also offer a special type of Unique called a Variant Unique. These special Uniques have many different variations that you can find. Two Variant Uniques are currently associated with the Rage of Morditas mechanic.

#### Withstand the Elements

Withstand the Elements is a Variant Unique for the Gloves item slot. In addition to its base Affixes, Withstand the Elements also drops with two extra Affixes from a pool exclusive to this item. These special Affixes interact with your Overcapped Cold or Physical Resistance in unique ways. You can obtain Withstand the Elements through Rage of Morditas encounters as well as from slaying Morditas or Pinnacle Morditas.

#### Unsated Rage

Unsated Rage is a Variant Unique for the Ring item slot. In addition to its base Affixes, it includes one Affix that matches one of the different Bloodrage Buffs. The only Bloodrage Buff not included is Reptilian Blood Rage, which spawns Loot Lizards. This means you can find 27 possible Bloodrage Effects on your Unsated Rage.

Some of these Bloodrage Effects are considered their own Subskills. If your Unsated Rage contains one of these Affixes with a Subskill, the tooltip for that Subskill is shown on the item tooltip.

You can find Unsated Rage by completing Rage of Morditas encounters, or by slaying Morditas or Pinnacle Morditas.

#### Variant Unique Special Ritual Interactions

When you find Withstand the Elements or Unsated Rage on a fully refreshed Rage of Morditas Reward Panel, Rituals can affect it in different ways. Frozen Rituals performed on a separate item rerolls the Unique's Variant Affix. Additionally, Bloody Rituals performed on a different item give a chance to add Legendary Potential to the item or Corrupt the Variant Unique.

## Morditas Progression

Rage of Morditas
As you complete Rage of Morditas encounters in the Monolith of Fate, you also make progress toward unlocking three exclusive Woven Echoes associated with this mechanic. These Woven Echoes are the path to challenging Morditas and eventually Pinnacle Morditas. The Morditas Activity panel of the Nexus tracks your progress.

### Unlocking the Morditas Woven Echoes

Rage of Morditas encounters in the Monolith of Fate contribute to an overall meta progression which ends with a fight against Morditas. To reach Morditas, though, you have to first unlock the two preceding Woven Echoes by slaying enemies in Rage of Morditas encounters. The Morditas Activity interface in the Nexus displays your current progress. Campaign encounters do not contribute to this progression.

You unlock the three Morditas Woven Echoes by participating in Rage of Morditas encounters.

- Site of Carnage (750 Kills) - Fight waves of Wengari.
- Blood of Farwood (2,000 Kills) - Defeat Yrun, Champion of Morditas.
- Circle of Frozen Blood (4,000 Kills) - Go to battle against Morditas, son of Heorot.

Morditas Woven Echo Progression

### Anger

Anger is a part of the Morditas Monolith of Fate progress and can be tracked in the Morditas Activity interface in the Nexus. It increases as you kill enemies during Monolith of Fate Rage of Morditas encounters. This mechanic affects all three Morditas Woven Echoes. The higher your Anger, the higher the difficulty and rewards. If this difficulty becomes too high, you can freely reduce your Anger level through the Morditas Activity interface in the Nexus.

Rage of Morditas Anger Bar

### Circle of Frozen Blood

The third and final Morditas Woven Echo, Circle of Frozen Blood, unlocks after 4,000 Rage of Morditas Kills. This Woven Echo contains the standard Morditas Boss encounter. As with the other two Woven Echoes before it, Anger affects its difficulty and rewards. Defeating Morditas here rewards the Demigod's Ascendance Woven Echo, which unlocks Pinnacle Morditas.

## Pinnacle Morditas

Rage of Morditas
Demigod's Ascendance is the Woven Echo that unlocks the fight with Pinnacle Morditas. You can obtain this by defeating the standard Morditas boss encounter in Circle of Frozen Blood. Demigod's Ascendance requires 400 Corruption to place into your Echo Web.

The Pinnacle version of Morditas is more difficult than the standard Morditas fight and does not scale with Corruption. It is positioned between Aberroth and Uber Aberroth in difficulty.

### Pinnacle Rewards

Morditas' Vengeance is a Unique Spear exclusive to the Pinnacle Morditas loot table. It lets Health Leech continue to accumulate while at Full Health. This allows stored or active Leech to continue replenishing Health, should you fall below Full Health. Morditas' Vengeance lets effects that depend on Active Health Leech continue functioning even while at Full Health.

In addition to this, Pinnacle Morditas can also drop the Variant Uniques: Withstand the Elements and Unsated Rage.

## Weaver Tree

Rage of Morditas
The Rage of Morditas mechanic has three associated Weaver Tree Nodes that affect how often it appears for you, and how it functions.

- Ubiquity of Rage makes Echoes more likely to contain Rage of Morditas encounters.
- Seekers of Ice and Blood makes Rage of Morditas specific Uniques and Item Subtypes significantly more common, at the cost of making enemies in Phase Two deal More Damage.
- Portents of Blood replaces one random Phase Two enemy with a random Omen and causes a pile of Corrupted Items to drop at the end of the encounter.

## Summary

Rage of Morditas
- You begin Rage of Morditas encounters by locating and interacting with Blood Crystals.
- When the encounter begins, a countdown starts. You can extend this timer by killing enemies. Your goal is to slay 200 enemies before the timer expires.
- As you take down enemies, you gain Bloodrage Charges at certain kill thresholds.
- When the timer expires, you are encircled by an arena, where you must fight revived versions of every enemy killed during the first phase.
- Completing a Rage of Morditas encounter spawns a Blood-Filled Crystal, which you may interact with to claim or manipulate your Rewards.
- The Rage of Morditas encounter has exclusive Item Subtypes and Variant Uniques.
- Three associated Woven Echoes unlock as you participate in these encounters, which culminate in a fight against Morditas.
- Defeating Morditas rewards you with a Demigod's Ascendance Woven Echo, which you can place on a 400+ Corruption Echo Web to challenge Pinnacle Morditas. Pinnacle Morditas is between Aberroth and Uber Aberroth in difficulty.
